subject: Darwin's bark spider
title: A Spider Smaller Than a Coin Builds Webs Across Whole Rivers

scenes.text: A spider with a body under an inch long builds webs across rivers.
Darwin's bark spider lives in the forests of Madagascar, and it was only described in 2010.
Its anchor thread can stretch up to 25 meters, from one riverbank to the other.
The web hanging from it can cover nearly three square meters, the biggest orb webs known.
The secret is its silk: tougher than any other spider's, and over ten times tougher than Kevlar.
So the river isn't in its way. It's the hunting ground.

description:
Darwin's bark spider, described in 2010 from Madagascar, strings anchor threads up to 25 meters across rivers and lakes.
Its orb webs can reach about 2.8 square meters, and its silk is the toughest biological material studied, over 10 times tougher than a similar piece of Kevlar.
Would you walk into one of these webs?
first_comment: A web from one riverbank to the other. Would you rather meet this spider or a tarantula?
